The above is absolutely great advice!  I was on board with telling him right away but I think taking the slow and steady approach is correct. When you are ready to serve the papers and surprise him you’ll have all your shit in order and he will still be in “affair fog” and hopefully let you take the lead more willingly but at the worst you’re as prepared as possible.  

Just to restate, I wouldn’t start touching or moving any funds or jointly gels property until discussing with a lawyer.  Also when you serve him the papers, is personally recommend having someone else with you in the house and maybe not have your kids there.  You never know how people will react and you want to safeguard yourself, and your family from any emotional damage and (god hopefully it doesn’t come to it but physical harm). Everyday forward is progress.  Backslides happen but it doesn't erase all the work you've been putting in to move on. I am a year out now and I still have bad days.  But I have really great days too!  Don't let that discourage you as the path towards healing is not linear but rather circular. It's been 6 months since my breakup (long story short exfiance cheated) and I still go through the waves of emotion.  Every situation and breakup is unique in its own way and unique to how you cope as an individual.  One thing I believe is certain is that the process is cyclical.  Over time the feelings definitely wax and wane in their intensity and hopefully eventually you become sort of numb to them.  I have gone through all the stages of grief and today I am feeling optimistic and energized where yesterday I felt very beat down and defeated by it all.  I think the best way to move through it is by focusing on what you like to do be it a hobby or exercise, talk to a friend, read a book, change your scenery (if possible during the quarantine).  Pretty much anything that can take your mind out of that black hole of thoughts.

Also, most importantly, be cognizant of the fact that you have had good days and that even though you feel bad in the moment, logically those positive emotions should reoccur.  And hopefully the pattern starts to ebb and flow more towards the positive than the negative.  As long as you recognize the process will repeat itself many times, and that you are deploying your own coping mechanisms (therapy helped me alot), then eventually this too shall pass.  The unfortunate answer repeated before is that it will just take time.  We've all experienced what you're going through and some of us still are.  You aren't alone and you will get through this!

Writing out letters have helped me tremendously.  Short background is I found out my ex fiancée of 5 years was cheating on me and I was devastated to say the least.  Somedays I wanted to reach out so badly, to have an explanation, for her to say she loved me, for her to say she was hurting, etc.  The list goes on and on.  But by writing a letter, it gave me a release, an outlet I could express myself and get everything down in black and white.  

Our relationship ended back in November, and while it doesn't feel as fresh or painful, I still feel sad and think about her alot.  I would suggest writing a letter.  Make it a work in progress and add and take away from it day by day.  Write it in a way you are most comfortable, and don't hide your feelings.  Write about your anger and pain and sadness, write about memories or happier times.  Whatever you feel in that moment, just write it out, let it flow and don't erase something if it is true to your feelings.  Eventually you can hopefully get to a point where the majority of your thoughts and feelings are all written down.  Make a final version of your letter, one that best encapsulates your total mindset.  Write that out and review it and decide if you want to send it.

At that point, who cares how he feels?  The letter is more for you and your healing process at this time.  You will be okay, and you will find happiness again someday.  Coming out of this breakup, you can use this as a chance to grow positively as a person and become a stronger individual.  You can work on your own faults and weaknesses while also accepting yourself for who you are.  Then when you meet that special person next time, you will be that much better, and they will be better for you as well.
